Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: Chronic non-specific neck or arm pain of unknown etiology
Cervical degenerative disc disease without radiculopathy or myelopathy

Required findings: Patient reports unilateral arm pain, paresthesia, or weakness consistent with a cervical nerve root distribution; pain ≥6/10 persisting >12 weeks despite conservative therapy.
Objective neurologic exam demonstrating sensory loss, diminished reflexes, or motor weakness in the affected myotome.
MRI or CT of the cervical spine showing foraminal or lateral recess stenosis with nerve root compression concordant with clinical findings.
Failure of ≥6 weeks of documented conservative management (physical therapy, oral NSAIDs, muscle relaxants, or epidural steroid injection).
Patient must be nicotine‑free for ≥6 weeks (cotinine test) and have no uncontrolled psychiatric disorder that would impair postoperative rehabilitation.
Patient exhibits gait disturbance, hand clumsiness, or upper motor neuron signs (hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign) attributable to cervical spinal cord compression.
Neurologic exam confirming motor weakness, spasticity, or sensory level consistent with cervical myelopathy.
MRI of the cervical spine demonstrating spinal cord signal change or compression at the relevant level.
Documented trial of ≥6 weeks of conservative therapy without functional improvement.
Nicotine cessation ≥6 weeks verified by cotinine testing and stable behavioral health status.

Non-Indications: Anterior cervical discectomy/corpectomy and fusion performed without meeting general guideline criteria for urgent/emergent conditions.
Procedure performed for chronic non‑specific neck or arm pain of unknown etiology.
Cervical degenerative disc disease without radiculopathy or myelopathy.
Anterior cervical discectomy/corpectomy performed without accompanying cervical fusion.
Anterior cervical osteotomy or vertebral column resection performed without satisfying the specific osteotomy criteria.
Anterior endoscopic cervical disc/nerve root decompression (including Jho procedure and Cervical Deuk Laser Disc Repair) considered experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Important criteria & exceptions: Nicotine use must be documented as absent for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery; verification via serum or urine cotinine level ≤10 ng/mL.
Active, unmanaged behavioral health disorders (e.g., uncontrolled depression, anxiety, substance use) must be stabilized before surgery; documentation of a recent psychiatric evaluation is required.
If urgent/emergent neurological compromise exists, the general guideline timeframes for conservative therapy may be waived.
Repeat fusion or adjacent segment disease requires documentation of prior fusion at an adjacent level performed ≥12 months earlier.
Documentation required: Comprehensive history and physical note detailing symptoms, pain scores, functional limitations, and neurologic exam findings.
Cervical spine MRI (or CT if MRI contraindicated) report showing level‑specific neural element compression concordant with clinical presentation.
Flexion‑extension cervical X‑rays demonstrating segmental instability when indicated.
Operative report of any prior cervical surgery (fusion, disc arthroplasty) including level(s) and date of procedure.
Physical therapy and/or occupational therapy records confirming ≥6 weeks of conservative management, including dates, modalities, and patient response.
Pharmacy records showing prescription of NSAIDs, muscle relaxants, or oral steroids during the conservative care period.
Laboratory cotinine test result (serum or urine) confirming nicotine‑free status.
Behavioral health evaluation note confirming stability of psychiatric conditions and readiness for postoperative rehabilitation.
